hypothesis: the identity guard compares console fingerprints against a different key TYPE than the one it scans (ed25519 vs rsa vs ecdsa)
falsifier: if the guard only ever accepts an exact ed25519 fingerprint and every successful lease matched exactly the scanned ed25519 key, type confusion cannot cause a false accept; B1f is then a mismatch of the published ed25519 pins or of untyped extra fingerprints

code_read.accept: exact SHA256 of the scanned ed25519 key in the published pin set (console_pin.wait_for_pin)
code_read.pin_set: full 'ssh-ed25519 <b64>' keys plus SHA256 fingerprints on lines labelled ED25519 or carrying no RSA/ECDSA label; RSA/ECDSA-labelled lines excluded
code_read.unknown_type: an unlabelled fingerprint of unknown type counts as a published pin; if it differs, the guard refuses (fail-closed)

measured_notes: every console published exactly 2 pins (n=6 receipts); in the 4 accepted leases the scanned ed25519 was one of them
the extra pin is different on every lease and is not the operator client key (compared by fingerprint equality, not printed)
B1f lease 57431305: neither of its 2 pins equals the scanned ed25519; raw console text was not retained by the operator, so the extra pins' key types are UNKNOWN
a prior audit (blackwell_fields_phase_20261022/provision/hostkey_publication_audit.json) shows the console prints the ED25519 fingerprint line and the full ssh-ed25519 key of the same host
verdict: NOT a type-comparison defect: the guard never accepts a different type (falsifier holds). B1f is either a genuine ed25519 mismatch or a refusal caused by two untyped non-ed25519 fingerprints before the ed25519 line appeared; with the console text not retained this is UNDETERMINED (INFERRED either way). Guard decision left unchanged (fail-closed).
change: operator-side evidence only: each polled console is kept privately in the operator workspace and its host-key lines (public fingerprints/keys and their type labels) are exported, so the next refusal can be classified; the guard source and decision are unchanged
